authority: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India

description.en: The One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) scheme enables ration card holders to purchase their entitled subsidized foodgrains from any Fair Price Shop (FPS) in India, regardless of the state that issued the ration card. This is facilitated through ePoS (electronic Point of Sale) machines at FPS using Aadhaar-based biometric authentication via the Integrated Management of Public Distribution System (IM-PDS). The scheme particularly benefits migrant workers and their families who move across states for employment. No separate application is needed — any existing ration card with Aadhaar seeding automatically qualifies for portability.

verifiedConditions.claim: The beneficiary must hold a valid ration card issued by any state or union territory under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013.
The ration card and its member details must be seeded (linked) with Aadhaar numbers. Aadhaar seeding is essential for biometric authentication at the ePoS machines at Fair Price Shops.
The beneficiary must be covered under NFSA as either Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) household or Priority Household (PHH) category to avail subsidized foodgrains through portability.

unverifiedEligibility: State-specific additional entitlements (beyond NFSA) may or may not be portable across states.
Beneficiaries with biometric exceptions (elderly, disabled) may face challenges at ePoS authentication and might need to use iris-based authentication instead of fingerprint.
Temporary ration cards issued to migrant workers by some states may have limited portability features.

requirements.claim: A valid ration card issued by any state or union territory under NFSA. The ration card number is used to verify the beneficiary's entitlement in the central IM-PDS database.

Aadhaar number of the beneficiary, seeded to the ration card. Aadhaar-based biometric authentication (fingerprint or iris) is performed at the ePoS machine at the Fair Price Shop to verify the beneficiary's identity.
The Fair Price Shop must be equipped with a functional ePoS (electronic Point of Sale) device connected to the IM-PDS system for real-time transaction authentication and recording.

processInformation.claim: Ensure all family members on the ration card have their Aadhaar numbers linked (seeded) to the ration card. This is done at the local PDS office or through the state food department's portal. Aadhaar seeding is a one-time prerequisite.

Visit any Fair Price Shop (FPS) equipped with an ePoS machine anywhere in India. The beneficiary does not need to register or apply separately for portability — the system automatically recognizes Aadhaar-seeded ration cards from any state.

At the FPS, the beneficiary authenticates via Aadhaar biometric (fingerprint or iris scan) on the ePoS machine. The machine connects to IM-PDS to verify the beneficiary's entitlement and remaining quota for the month.

Upon successful authentication, the entitled quantity of foodgrains (rice, wheat, coarse grains) is dispensed at the subsidized rate. The transaction is recorded in real-time in the IM-PDS system, and the entitlement balance is updated across states.

output.claim: Subsidized foodgrains (wheat at Rs. 2/kg, rice at Rs. 3/kg, coarse grains at Rs. 1/kg for PHH; 35 kg per household per month for AAY) from any ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop in India. The entitlement is deducted from the beneficiary's monthly quota as maintained in the IM-PDS central database.

fees.applicability: No fee for availing ration portability under ONORC
fees.claim: There is no additional fee or charge for using the ration card portability feature under ONORC. The beneficiary pays only the standard subsidized price for foodgrains as prescribed under NFSA.

processingTime.applicability: Real-time transaction at ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop
processingTime.claim: The portability transaction is processed in real-time at the ePoS machine. Upon successful Aadhaar biometric authentication, foodgrains are dispensed immediately. No prior application or waiting period is involved.

sources.evidenceExcerpt: The IM-PDS portal provides real-time data on inter-state and intra-state portability transactions, ePoS machine deployment status, Aadhaar seeding coverage, and state-wise ONORC implementation progress. It is the central platform enabling ration card portability across India.
claimsSupported: Ration card portability across all states and UTs via ePoS machines.
Aadhaar-based biometric authentication required at FPS.
Real-time entitlement verification and transaction recording.
No separate application or registration needed for portability.
sources.uncertainty: Portal uptime and ePoS connectivity in remote areas may affect real-time transaction processing.

sources.title: One Nation One Ration Card — Department of Food and Public Distribution
sources.publisher: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: ONORC enables NFSA beneficiaries, especially migrant workers, to lift their entitled quota of foodgrains from any FPS in the country through Aadhaar authentication on ePoS devices. The scheme covers all 36 states and UTs. AAY families get 35 kg per household per month and PHH beneficiaries get 5 kg per person per month at subsidized rates.
claimsSupported: All 36 states and UTs are covered under ONORC.
AAY: 35 kg per household; PHH: 5 kg per person per month.
Subsidized rates: wheat Rs. 2/kg, rice Rs. 3/kg, coarse grains Rs. 1/kg.
Aadhaar seeding of ration cards is a prerequisite.
Scheme primarily benefits migrant workers and their families.
sources.uncertainty: State-specific additional entitlements beyond NFSA may not be available through portability. Exact number of ePoS-enabled FPS may vary.

limitations: Portability is limited to the NFSA entitlement only; state-specific additional subsidies or entitlements may not be portable across state borders.
Aadhaar biometric authentication is mandatory — beneficiaries with biometric issues (worn fingerprints, elderly) may face difficulties and need to use iris authentication.
Fair Price Shops in remote or poorly connected areas may have intermittent ePoS connectivity, affecting real-time transaction processing.
The monthly entitlement is shared across all locations — any quantity lifted at a different FPS reduces the remaining quota at the home-state FPS.
Migrant workers must ensure Aadhaar seeding is completed before migrating, as the seeding process requires visiting the local PDS office in the home state.
Non-NFSA beneficiaries (state-specific BPL or other categories not under NFSA) may not be covered under ONORC portability.

review.reviewReason: Core ONORC scheme details verified from DFPD and IM-PDS portal. State-level implementation specifics and ePoS coverage statistics need periodic verification.
nextReviewTrigger: Changes to NFSA entitlement quantities or subsidized prices.
Expansion of portability to cover state-specific schemes beyond NFSA.
Changes to biometric authentication methods or alternatives to Aadhaar.
Updates to ePoS machine deployment or IM-PDS platform changes.
